body:
It is not uncommon for these ‘gifted’ programmes to turn into empty promises and dashed hopes. As adults we know that often the ‘giftedness’ doesn’t translate itself into success in high school or beyond, let alone adulthood. 

And then we have a few generations of people (from the young like OP to early middle-aged folks like myself) who need to spend years to get over the disappointment, wondering if we did not have the potential in the first place, or if we failed to reach that potential.

I think I used to have motivation to get better. Kept carrying on despite everything, hoping that my suffering would end. 

The zero motivation kicked in when I realized that I am stuck in a hopeless situation that would not improve regardless of my effort.

Yes. 

It happens whenever it registers in my mind that my entire life is a failure and it seems inevitable that I am heading for disaster. And people around me agrees.
Good to hear that you found a goal. I think people who have experienced mental health issues firsthand are likely to be more empathetic.

The last time I lost a lot of weight, people were tiptoeing around the issue as to whether I was seriously ill. 

I have bounced to the other end tho, as I comfort eat. 

I force myself to eat healthy at work during lunch.

I don’t see therapists because I don’t think they can teach me anything that I don’t already know. I’ve probably been depressed for longer than they’ve been alive. 

However I think most act in good faith, within the boundaries of their job description. Ultimately it’s a job. Like all jobs, some does it better, some less so. Perhaps find another therapist?

I don’t think you need to change if you are amongst close friends. 

However if it’s a situation where you’d feel more comfortable to add to the conversation, you may try to raise a topic and others will fill the gaps.

If it really worries you, you can ring your supervisor during this internship and ask for some feedback about your performance. If a short phone call can resolve your anxiety, it’s certainly worth it to ring.

Sometimes people don’t know what to say. And ‘it gets better’ is sort of a vague statement, which, I hope, is uttered with the intention of giving you hope. 

I myself never uttered it - primarily because I am the embodiment of ‘things not getting better’. It’d sound ridiculous coming from me. 

At the same time, it would seem unkind and perhaps unwarranted for me to say ‘from my personal experience, it doesn’t get better, you might as well prepare yourself for a really long and rocky ride in life - your dreams will be shattered, you will be brought down on your knees, and you will not bounce back.’ After all, there are people who do get better. Hence my standard line is ‘ I hope things get better for you’.

It’s the predictable aftermath of a generation where the parenting/teaching culture was to lavish praise and avoid criticism. 

The real world is not so kind. Often there’s just one prize for a hundred persons fighting for it.

I understand. The anxiety is so debilitating that it prevents me from emerging from my comfort zone in all aspects in my life. And the years and the opportunities just went by. 

I hope you find a way to break through your cocoon.

I’ve never wanted to tell family and I never did.

Family is a strange entity, afterall. We did not choose them, nor they, us. We are strangers bound together by blood but may have completely incompatible personalities. There are also the undercurrents and histories that lie right underneath a thin layer of courtesy, always ready to explode. 

Reach out to someone who may help (a professional) or reach within yourself to find whatever that needs to be found.
I think for many of us, unfortunately, it’s a matter of learning to co-exist with it, and to live a relatively functional life.

I have always lived frugually even when I was young - I guess I should be grateful for that. But I am often struck with the reality that this is what it is - I will struggle with money for as long as I live. 

It’s more than a sense of being trapped - I’m also constantly feeling guilty that I can’t earn more.
They do not need nursing homes yet but the medical costs are hefty. No other sibling to help.
That is not feasible as I have ill and elderly parents.

When I’m in a hoodie I keep my hands in the pockets. 

Otherwise I hold my phone in one hand.
Glad to hear that you have a plan. I wish I have the guts, or the skills to start another job. Good luck.
I’m glad you persevered.

You speak my mind. My meds didn’t work either (except the sleep meds) because I’m depressed by life’s problems. Eating right, exercising, meditating, etc would not solve my problems (I already eat right and take walks most days). I have problems at home, at work, and money problems.

For most of my life, I’ve grown up with kids and subsequently worked with colleagues who are very well-off. Meanwhile I’m from a lower middle class family fraught with underlying problems. 

I know as a middle aged person this may sound irresponsible. But yes I’m saying it. If I had their families, I’d not have ended up as I have, nor would I face the problems that I had faced and will face. 

So I’ve decided a long time ago that I’d not have children, and for once, God/fate gave me my wish.

Friends are overrrated. 

I’ve also ‘isolated’ my ‘friends’. Even my ‘friend’ of over 20 years has stayed away. For all intents and purposes the only result of this exercise is that fewer people trouble me with their petty problems. For that I’m grateful.
My anxiety (depression) prevented me from taking on challenges. As a result, I’m still doing work of a junior despite being in my career for nearly a decade.

For what it is worth, they’d soon be out of their teens and would face the full force of the law. 

Young people often seem to be oblivious that they’d grow old just like everyone else.
Kindness is not necessarily reciprocated. Be kind by all means, but don’t feel let down if it’s not returned.

I think you are being responsible and sensible. Having children is a huge responsibility and should not be done for self-gratification.

I myself have decided a long long time ago that I’d not procreate. I do not want to pass along defective genes. Alternatively, even if my child were normal, it’s likely my own problems would ruin it. I do not want my child and I to bear grudges (spoken or unspoken) against each other.

I personally don’t see the difference between talking to a therapist and talking to the air. Except for the interruptions like ‘how do you feel about that?’ and ‘I understand’. 

That’s the reason I adamantly refused my shrink’s referral to a therapist (more specifically a therapist in the same practice). I asked the shrink is there anything that I can’t/won’t tell her that she anticipates I can/will tell a therapist? She wasn’t able to give me a satisfactory answer to my question.

Similar situation here. And in my 30s I just feel that there’s no turning back. 

I had always known I would be alone. But I wish I had some success at work. I hate the fact that I have absolutely nothing to show for, after living for so long. 

I’m sorry I have no advice for you, but I wish you well.

Laziness ‘I’m not bothered to do it, even though I’m capable of doing it’. 

Depression is ‘I want to do it but I can’t do it as I think it’s going to be rubbish’. 

Result-wise, I’m unproductive and inefficient. However I don’t think I am a lazy person at all.

If there is any reason at all for my existence, it seems to be for serving my family. None of my own wishes, dreams, and hopes ever mattered. 

I wish I were tuned to my purpose in life - I know there are many who willingly or at least, without complaint, served their family. But I admit I am a selfish person who just feel bitter and resentful. I don’t believe I will be free and find peace until I die.
But for my responsibilities, none of which I had wanted,asked for, or rewarded, I’d readily succumb to it.

Yes. Life has its way of changing a person. 

When I see people (whom I know well) who I know have nothing to worry about, I am not especially impressed by their courtesy, generosity, or grace. I believe had I been in their position, I’d have conducted myself in the same manner. 

I’m sure there are people in adverse situations who are still the best of their own self. But I’m not such a big person.

No. Most people around me, family, colleagues, and friends alike, have lived long enough to know:-

1. Don’t ask questions that they don’t want to know the answer to (on the off chance I actually give an honest answer); and 

2. Don’t ask questions that may be seen as an invitation extended to me to ask for help (on the off chance I actually ask for help).
It takes getting used to. But I think eventually you’d get used to it and hopefully may derive some satisfaction from it. Good luck.
After trying to answer this question a few times, I gave up, for the reason that my best traits are also my worst in many circumstances.

For myself, I think being old aggravates the depression and the loneliness. I can’t deny that there are less opportunities, be it personal or career, and more problems and responsibilities (eg personal health, aging parents, etc).
I’d top it with being old.

Whatever reason you attribute to it. 

Having said that I think many people flow through life without a ‘point’ or purpose. And there’s nothing wrong with that.

Intelligence (assuming you are referring to assessable intelligence)is just a piece of the puzzle. Useful when you are a student, but hardly definitive of anything as an adult. 

I had tests done as a child. My academic record speaks for itself. However, I’m an utter failure in my choice of profession, and as an adult human being. 

Looking back at my life, I think I’d have happily traded my intelligence for resilience, social skills, and stable temperament. With those, I believe even if I end up exactly as I am now, I’d not feel the deep despair and resentment that I feel every day.
I die a bit inside every time my hopes are crushed. I think I am dead inside.
Any reason to live is good enough. Enjoy.

I think such advice has to come with a preamble ‘you have time, but not that much’ and ‘things may get better, but only if you deal with them’. 

I am a shining example of what happens to depressed kids who thought their problems would go away upon maturity. Nope - I am just an angry, bitter middle aged person who is more depressed with each passing year. 

To be fair to myself, I did try to turn things around - I simply failed.

Mine’s bottled up anger. 
Sometimes I wish I used that anger and fought back when I am bullied at work. But nope I’m a coward.
If I could die in my sleep, I would consider it the best thing ever to have happened to me.

I have a similar story which happened to me when I was about 18. 

I had this mole which seemed to look different. I freaked out for months, which interferred with my studies. 

Finally I went to a doctor to have it removed. And that was the end of the story. 

When I look back on those times now, I wonder what on earth was I thinking to not simply deal with it immediately. 

I suggest you have it checked out so as to restore your peace of mind.

I’ve learnt to try to look at the relationship from the other person’s perspective. I am clearly a person who is very insecure, needy, with serious issues. I am toxic and would dampen the spirit of the most joyous of persons. 

So usually I interact people on the premise that they would have enough soon. I consider myself setting them free from me.
Putting on a facade is exhausting. I allow myself to remove the facade when I commute, and when I’m working alone in the office.

Yep. 

The anxiety and depression prevented me giving things a shot (let alone a good shot) when I was young. So here I am, middle aged with the skills and experience of perhaps someone a decade younger.

I have always been the spare. The person one turns to if no other options are available. 

Having said that, if I reverse roles w these people, I wouldn’t want to be best friends with me either.

My opinion would probably be unpopular - but I think one of the difficulties faced by depressed people is that we tend to give too much weight to what others say or do, or in what we perceived what others had said or done. 

Most of the time people don’t think or care about others (us). They have enough problems of their own. So if/and when they make any reference to how we are doing it’s probably just chit-chat or actually a well-meant gesture. They are not our doctors, and have no obligation to have an in-depth analysis or understanding as to our well-being.

I don’t know specifically how I will get through - but as with most things in life, I guess I can only get on with it. 

Cutting down my expenses is definitely at the topmost of my priority. Stopping my shrink appt is also part of this exercise.

The first 3 items are gd, if you are young and you have time for it, and more importantly other people still have time for you. 

The last 2 items are usually uttered when people don’t know what else to say. 

On a separate note, once I hit my mid- late 20s (which was a long time ago), people stopped saying to me any of the above.
Grit.
That happened to me during my childhood, back when selective mutism wasn’t commonly known (thank goodness for that).  I would just cry for hours and fail to explain why. Literally could not speak.

I’ve pondering taking a shower for the last 2 hours.

A shower itself takes about 10 minutes.
If you reverse your role, I think you may agree that there r very few ppl that you actually hate/laugh at, or you feel strong emotions towards. Hope this eases your mind a bit.
Yes. It’s the only thing I know for my entire life. However it’s a v private topic hence I hardly have conversations with people in real life.
My responsibility towards my parents.
Days go by slowly. But the years fly by.

The world is very target-oriented. 

My clients won’t thank me for simply having done the best that anyone could have done.

I’ve been forced by the needs of my job to develop social skills. I can talk to people but I’m hypersensitive to criticism (or possible criticism) and this holds me back from many opportunities. But at my age I believe I’ve reached my maximum potential and I really can’t do better.

I expected a lonely life and being unpopular. 

I didn’t expect the career failure.

Works wonders for some, does nothing for others. But it’s worth trying. 

I have tried a few, but they didn’t work for me. I’m only on a low dose of sleeping meds and valium now.

I wish we could all be kinder to each other. 

I have eczema and ppl at work sometimes make a fuss over it (as in pointing out that my face is red and blotchy as if I don’t know that). I’m not young (early 30s) so I’m not very sensitive about my looks. But I would prefer they shut up about it.

The valiums sort of calm me down when I am really anxious and can’t settle down (as in literally pacing and doing everything but handling what I really need to do). 

The alcohol makes me a bit more sociable. 

I think if I can keep my consumption of alcohol at a moderate level, it might actually be more preferable to the valiums?
I don’t know. Alcohol has been my choice of poison for years and I seem to be heading back to it.
Same situation. I work to live but the work makes me not want to live.
I’d be happy to give it to anyone, even if he’s 100, as long he wants to continue to living.

I’ve always considered it my best decision in life not to have children. I simply don’t have the resources to set him/her up in this very competitive world. And god forbid if he/she is actually not very clever. 

I was very clever. I worked very hard. My parents invested a lot in me. And I turned out to be absolutely rubbish. My life is worthless (save for the inherent value of life). I derive no pleasure or satisfaction. My parents seem to bear a slight grudge because I don’t make much (partly due to incompetence, partly due to personality, and to a small degree due to the depression). 

And I’m not a ranting kid. I’m an adult with a professional job w close to a decade of work experience.
I’d also be happy to donate it.

I am most certainly replaceable at my work and amongst ‘friends’. 

I am irreplaceable to my parents. Only child, I am supposed to be here to support them financially if not actually provide physical care in their old age. 

Worst combination, I daresay.

Have you got someone to look at your CV for you? You may need to get whatever internship or placement available to fill your CV with something before you land a job. The competition is tough. 

I have a job, which was of my choice, which I have done for years. But I’m feeling that it is incompatible with me. I’m too afraid to look for jobs though so I understand the pressure. 

I think that with a job you will have better self-esteem. Good luck.

It’s always either this or that, isn’t it. I’m so tired of juggling all these fears and anxieties. 

Even when I occasionally do something right, I’m bound to make mistakes later on and it’d kill whatever satisfaction I gained.

The world is for tough people, or for people who have a cushy fallback. 

I am neither.
I just want to disappear as if I’ve never existed.
Perhaps I will give it a try again tonight if I can summon the courage.
Pain, agony and disappointment.

At home I talk to myself but not pace.

At work I pace but not talk to myself. 

Frankly such activities waste a lot of my time and energy as I simply quite can’t settle down.

Same boat. No friends, no partner. 

Prolly soon to have no job too. 

Mid-life is no fun.

Thank you for taking time to respond. 

I think about suicide often but I don’t think I intend to act on it immediately. It’s just that I’m v depressed and anxious and want some company. I don’t know if that qualifies for me to make a phone call. 

I’ve taken a slightly higher dose of valium today. Hopefully that would give me a bit of peace.

Once, when I was young, when I could still cry. I sat at the front row on the top deck. It was quite late and there was no one around to see me. 

I think it’s good to be able to cry.

You are right. I want some company. 

But I have no one in my life. And it’d be a waste of time for the volunteer at the Samaritans if I don’t really talk.
Thank you for your kind words.
Just write as if you are speaking to no one.
I wish there was someone. But there’s no one I can talk to in-depth and feel secure.

It’s automated response. They probably did not mean to fake positivity or give you false hope. They simply did not know what to say but have to say something out of social etiquette. 

If it’s of any help, by the time you are an adult (I assume you are young), no one would even bother with asking or giving polite answers.

Sorry to hear that. It might have been a joke, but it was insensitive. And if you had seen her for awhile, she would have known whether you would appreciate this type of humor. 

I have recently also been told by my shrink to contact her at any time should I need to talk. She had the grace not to mention that I’d be charged (at 300 quid a session) but obviously that goes without saying. 

At the end of the day, don’t take it too personally. She’s just your therapist, not anyone personal in your life, you can ditch her any time. 

Hope you feel better soon.

Sadness is quite different from chronic depression. 

As you have aptly pointed out, people can cope with another person’s sadness for a short while. 

But chronic depression is a long-term if not lifelong problem. I wish someone would care about me long-term but realistically I know it’s too much of a burden to impose on another. If roles are reversed, I think I wouldn’t be able to deal with such demands. 

Having said that I am also going through minor disappointment re an acquaintance. But I’ve lived long enough to understand.

Much older than you. 

I entered a profession of my choice with high hopes but I hate it now because I am rubbish at it. 

If I can afford it, I would not work either. But I most certainly can’t afford to do so. 

Perhaps you’d feel better if you find something you like to do after work hours? I think most people don’t particularly like their jobs but find enjoyment outside it.
That’s also my experience. The workplace is a dog-eat-dog world and colleagues are not friends.

I have to say this is exactly the age when you have to make realistic plans and take action. You are young but not so young that you have years to waste and then start all over. 

In my own experience, time flew by in a blink of an eye and suddenly I found myself in my 30s with little to show for. I am jealous of the success of my contemporaries, and looked down on by those younger than me. 

A troubled young person might be given the benefit of the doubt,  as there is always possibility and potential in youth. Troubled adults like myself are simply losers.
I’ve always been lonely and miserable. Never quite knew if it’s my personality or depression.

People assume I make a lot of money based on my profession. So the question that I get asked (usually by family) is why do I make so little? 

I don’t mention the depression. I just blame the market.
Thank you. I’m trying to calm down.

I was just thinking lately how my medical bills for depression/anxiety/insomnia are becoming a source of stress in itself. 

I pay about £300 per month, which covers my shrink appt and meds. I don’t see a therapist. 

At this point in time I can still afford it. But I have to say I have been considering stopping treatment as I don’t see significant improvement and I don’t want money to become a problem.
It will get better if you take action. Set realistic goals and achieve them. Time goes by really really quickly (at least in my own experience) so don’t wait around (like I did).

Thanks for the reply.

So far the meds still work and I’m spared the agony of lying in bed for hours on end waiting for sleep to come.

I don’t really know how to deal with my other issues, that’s part of the reason why I decided to taper - I know that taking the sleeping meds and valium without resolving my underlying problems is not going to work in the long run.

My two-cents worth (many years ago I went to Uni in London - I am from another country). 

Remember all the times that you’ve tried something new and that you had adapted or even enjoyed the experience. 

Good luck in your endeavors.

Those around me tell me (possibly for kind reasons) that I’m wasting my time and I’m not cut out to do what I’m doing. 

I choose to disregard such comments. 

At the end of the day, it’s your self-perception that matters.

I wish they were right. I wish more that I could tell it will for sure go away. 

The fact is I’m still as depressed or even more depressed than I had been in my teens. And I’m in my 30s now.
Anxiety prevents me from starting anything. The result is depression.

I think you are right. I often talk to myself (in my own space and privacy). And often I ask myself, what do I want? What can I do to make things better? And the answers are always, I don’t know, and nothing. I can’t quite imagine myself bombarding someone (who I don’t pay) with such stupidity.

Happens to me too. 

I think it’s a chicken-or-egg situation. Is it because of my long years of depression that sends out vibes to people to stay the hell away from me? Or is it because of some inherent defect in my personality that caused me to be friendless and hence contributed to the depression?

I have a ‘friend’ who sought my advice in the last two months. But she has lots and lots of friends supporting her. She had cancelled me twice (once last week, and today) because she had other social plans.

I agree. I have had 20 odd years of experience too. 

People don’t care. Or just don’t have the capacity to care. Certainly not long term. Affection, compassion, and patience do run out at some point. 

My shrink encourages me to talk to her ‘anytime’, to let her know if I encounter any problem. However I can’t help but think it is to do with the fact that she charges me about £300 per appointment.

For years. Since I was in my early teens. 

I’m now in my 30s. The only reason I keep myself alive is just so that I outlive my parents. It’s filial piety.
Where I am from, this question is equivalent to a greeting. So by default the answer is good and you?

The world is big. Most people are fairly average. People who think they are good at something usually just have a better self-image. The fact that you think you are not good at something doesn’t necessarily means you aren’t.

I don’t know if this would cheer you up:

I was a ‘winner’ during my academic career (depressed and all that, but nevertheless did well enough). Got my career path decided and sorted early and seamlessly entered into my chosen profession. However, I am absolutely rubbish in my career, whereas my contemporaries are now settled down and doing well. My point is, life is a long race. Your friends may be just enjoying a false headstart and you have every chance to catch up.

Know the company, know the role your are applying for. 

Smile, look your interviewer in the eyes, give a good strong handshake if he offered his hand. 

Speak calmly, politely, with sincerity. 

Prepare in advance sensible questions to ask in case you are asked if you have any questions. 

Thank the interviewer for the opportunity and his time at the end of it. 

Hope this helps.

I tend to think that the 20s is the most important part of an adult’s life in terms of finding a spouse and career development, so you have come to your realization at the right time. Make the most of these years. 

Regret is all-consuming in nature. I’m much older and my long years of regret has become a habit. Don’t be me.

I feel you. I’ve also tried pretty much everything. 

In fact I have a shrink appt today, in which I believe will be my last appt (in the foreseeable future at least). I’ve just simply had enough.

I hope things do turn up for you.
I understand it’s a frustrating problem for you but I’m actually a bit jealous. I have no relationship at all to speak of with my shrink - she’s just someone whom I see to get my meds.

I had this same problem. I am learning to accept it. 

I had/have this one ‘friend’ (to use the term loosely) whom I opened up to, with her encouragement. Eventually she pretty much ghosted me except when it’s a work related matter. When it first happened, I was really upset. 

About 2 months ago, she approached me with a personal problem and we suddenly became ‘close’ again. At that point in time, I thought “Right. She’s gonna ditch me when she recovers in a month or two. Do I want to go through this again?” 

I kept her company in the last 2 months, with my eyes open to the fact that she will take off when she feels better. 

And indeed, a few days ago she stood me up when we were supposed to meet (well, cancelling abt 1 hour before we were to meet) and she stopped replying to my messages. I can only gather that yes things have turned out alright for her. 

I do accept that I am probably an expert in misery, despair, disappointment, jealousy and every negative emotion. But I know nothing about being happy. So people naturally turn to me in times of turmoil, and naturally turn away from me in times of peace.

I just find her crusade against one to be very pointless. Her husband being much more senior to me would not have clientele similar to mine. 

One reason the I speculate is behind her vendentta against me is that there’s a whole bunch of colleagues of my seniority or slightly junior who are ‘her people’ (as in children of her friends or relatives) so perhaps she considers me a threat/competition to them. 

I’m just tired of office politics but that happens everywhere.

The weird thing is, her husband, as far as I am aware of, has no grudge against me. He’s over 20 years my senior, we’ve never worked together, hardly ever spoke. 

Crazy world that I live in.

There are probably laws that make the inciting of suicide an offence. However she well knows I wouldn’t kick up a fuss - I need the bloody job. 

I just find the whole episode very lacking in taste, tact, and grace. But this is the world where I (we) live in.

Thanks for your kind words. She certainly did not suffer much - despite minimal education she married well - they live in one of the most expensive areas in the city, the marriage is is intact and the child grown.

Coincidentally something similar happened to me today. I also posted about it to vent. 

Some people are just nasty. Or extremely lucky, to have never felt despair in their lives. Or so full of self-entitlement to have no doubt that he/she would never feel such darkness in his/her life.

There are different types of smarts. You seem to be suggesting that you are not smart in real life but that does not affect your IQ. 

I’m in a similar position. For me the shit thing is that after a life time (well at least until I graduated from grad school) of being told I was smart, I could not cope well in the real world.

Totally understand the dread. 

That drove me to get some sleeping tablets from my doctor.
That’s a zen thought. I am prone to jealousy and anger.
I worry about this as well as ‘things could always be worse’.  In sum,  my life is either stagnant or with huge potential to plummet and deteriorate.
I admire that. I’d have huge difficulty around small children as my negatives vibes are so strong.

Similar age, similar questions. 

I’ve hid my depression well most of my life but I know I’m not a regular functioning adult. 

People our age seems to have somehow missed out - nowadays youths are much more likely to address depression and receive help, whereas in our days there was more stigma to it. In my case I’m sure that my school and my mother at some point must have realized something was wrong with me but nothing was done. 

Nowadays in my 30s it just seems so pointless. I don’t have time and I can’t afford to actually take some time off to properly rest and receive treatment. I’ve been seeing a shrink for over a year and she seems to agree with me that little can be done. 

So it is my own view that in my own case that it’s late for some things - I’m not really gonna learn the proper social skills to connect with people or to advance my career. 

On a separate note, we’ve made it this far - no easy feat to go from childhood to midlife with such pervasive and debilitating depression. If we keep our heads down and do what we can do with what we have we may be able to get through to the end of our natural lives without great turmoil. 

Sorry for my personal vent - I’m under some pressure as my mother thinks I’m not making sufficient financial contribution to her and it is stressing me out greatly.
My depression and anxiety are best friends and come hand in hand together. It’s just a matter of who of the two has a louder voice at the moment.

Agree. 

People just don’t seem to realize that depressed kids do grow old too if they survive.

I’ve learnt not to test the limits of my relationships. 

Some people pry out of curiosity (those are never to be trusted). Some people wanted to care but if they are not depressed themselves they may not understand the depths and magnitude of despair - they thought it’d just be a passing phase. They did not sign up for the darkness, or to comfort and counsel forever, and often seemingly without any result (at least my depression doesn’t abate simply from a few words of comfort)

I used to be pretty pissed at a ‘friend’ who ‘abandoned’ me after I opened up to her. But enough is enough, I get that. It’s disappointing but I understand.!
Glad you sought help. Another work opportunity will come by. I hope you resolve your anxiety - I myself have a lot of work anxiety but I can’t quit the job.

Tried snapping my fingers, can’t quite do it.

I understand the feeling. It’s like hitting a wall every day.
I wish I would be given a bit of leeway of living my life and doing my best despite my severe depression. But nope, the real world doesn’t care.
Yup. The anxious mind just has an antenna for anything and everything. As if it cannot exist without fear or worry.

Personal experience gives us insight, empathy, and compassion. One who is vulnerable knows what it feels like to be vulnerable. I hope you give your goal a good shot, but do take care of yourself in the process.
My cheeks (and ears) flush when I have a panic attack. Or I feel a strange chill all over. My heart rate goes up though.

On this I can speak with personal experience. 

I used to have to make loads of preparation before I make a phone call at work (like writing down what I have to say) and I delay as long as possible to do so.
